name: ai-chatbot-support-tickets
title: AI Chatbot Support Tickets
description: Synthetic IT help desk ticket dataset built for a Tableau proof-of-concept dashboard comparing AI chat-bot support against human IT escalation. Delivered as two workbooks - Actuals (2021-2026) and Projections (2022-2026) - sharing an identical 21-column schema for unioning.
license: Synthetic data - free for demo, training, and portfolio use
disclaimer: All records are programmatically generated. No real people, tickets, or organizations are represented.
referenceDateNote: Treated as 'today'. All open-ticket ages (Days Open) are measured against this date.
dashboardPurpose: Compare AI-resolved tickets against tickets escalated to human IT support
Rank the six AI bots against each other by closure rate (Actual table only)
Compare open AI tickets, open escalation tickets, and closed tickets
Analyze ticket severity mix (High / Medium / Low) and its effect on escalation
Support Plan-vs-Actual comparison via the paired Projection table

escalationRule.description: A ticket escalates to a human IT processor once it remains open past a severity-driven day threshold.

ticketLifecycle: Every ticket starts with an AI bot assigned (Assigned AI Bot always populated in the Actual table).
On escalation, Escalated Date and Assigned IT Processor are populated, Current Assigned Support flips from 'AI Bot' to 'IT Support', and Current Assigned Name becomes the human processor.
Days Open = Closed Date - Created Date for closed tickets, or referenceDate - Created Date for open tickets.

statusAlignment.description: Ticket Status, Ticket Sub-Status, and Ticket Processor Status are always mutually consistent.

openBacklog.note: All open tickets fall within 90 days of the reference date by construction, concentrating them in Jul-Sep 2026.

businessRules.requestorConsistency: Each of the 12500 requestors has a fixed name, ID, and office location across all their tickets. Requestor ID is the identity key; duplicate full names exist by design.

escalationModel.description: Escalation likelihood is driven by the assigned bot's closure rate and the ticket's severity; Days Open is then generated on the correct side of the severity threshold. A weaker bot leaves more tickets unresolved past the threshold, so they escalate.
escalationModel.consistency: The day-based escalation rule still holds exactly - Days Open, Escalated Date, and the status fields never contradict each other.
escalationModel.severityWeighting: High-severity tickets escalate about 2.5x more often than Low/Medium within each bot's overall rate.

september2026Reduction.description: September 2026 created-ticket volume was reduced in two passes.
september2026Reduction.method: First pass cut 29%, scaling the open backlog by the same 0.71 factor (open tickets are overwhelmingly September-created). Second pass removed a further 1,000 tickets from September's closed bucket only, leaving the 2,272-ticket open backlog intact.
september2026Reduction.compositionNote: September now contains 2,058 open and 1,038 closed tickets, so roughly two thirds of the month is open backlog. Neighbouring months are almost entirely closed.

resources.name: actuals
resources.temporalNote: 2026 is partial (Jan 1 - Sep 30) because the reference date is 2026-10-01.
resources.formatting: Bold frozen header row, autofilter enabled, Arial throughout. Dates stored as real Excel date values (yyyy-mm-dd), Days Open as a true number.

resources.name: projections

methodology.2026: Annualizes the Actual Jan-Sep 2026 run rate (31000 / 9 * 12 = 41333), since a full-year plan cannot sensibly fall below nine months of realized actuals.
methodology.2022-2025: Each year's own Actual volume target used as the planning baseline, with independent random jitter (+/-3% at year level, +/-15% month to month), so Plan and Actual land close but never match exactly.

resources.allClosedNote: A projection represents expected completed volume for capacity planning, not a live open backlog. Open, User Feedback, and open-side processor statuses never appear in this table.
resources.unchangedNote: Left untouched by the v1.1.0 bot-rate change. Carries no Assigned AI Bot value, so per-bot analysis does not apply.
resources.formatting: Bold frozen header row, autofilter enabled, Arial throughout. Dates stored as real Excel date values (yyyy-mm-dd), Days Open as a true number.

schema.note: Identical across both tables. Column order is fixed and must be preserved for a clean union.

fields.name: Ticket ID
fields.description: Unique ticket identifier.

fields.name: Requestor Name
fields.description: First and last name of the employee who submitted the ticket. Drawn from culture-grouped name pools weighted to loosely resemble each office city's population mix. Duplicate names exist by design.

fields.name: Requestor ID
fields.description: Stable unique identifier for the requestor. This is the identity key, not the name.

fields.name: Office Location
fields.description: US office city the requestor belongs to. Fixed per requestor across all their tickets.

fields.name: Team Name
fields.description: IT team that owns the ticket. Currently assigned independently of Issue Category.

fields.name: Issue Category
fields.description: High-level issue grouping oriented to AI chat support requests.

fields.name: Issue Type
fields.description: Detailed issue classification nested under Issue Category. Each Issue Type carries its own Ticket Type and Severity distribution, so those fields correlate with the nature of the issue.
fields.hierarchy: Issue Category > Issue Type (each Issue Type belongs to exactly one Issue Category)

fields.name: Ticket Type
fields.description: Whether the ticket is a service request or a reported problem. Weighted per Issue Type.

fields.name: Severity
fields.description: Business impact level. Drives the escalation threshold (High escalates after 7 days, Medium/Low after 20).

fields.name: Ticket Status
fields.description: Top-level ticket state.

fields.name: Ticket Sub-Status
fields.description: Detailed state within Ticket Status. Adds the 'User Feedback' waiting-on-user nuance that Ticket Processor Status omits.

fields.name: Ticket Processor Status
fields.description: Clean AI-vs-escalation cut crossed with open/closed state. Recommended field for AI-vs-human comparisons.

fields.name: Created Date
fields.description: Date the ticket was submitted. Weekend volume is intentionally down-weighted.

fields.name: Escalated Date
fields.description: Date the ticket was handed from the AI bot to a human IT processor. Populated only for escalated tickets.

fields.name: Closed Date
fields.description: Date the ticket was closed. Populated for closed tickets only.

fields.name: Days Open
fields.description: Closed Date minus Created Date for closed tickets; reference date (2026-10-01) minus Created Date for open tickets.

fields.name: Assigned AI Bot
fields.description: AI chat bot that initially handled the ticket. Always populated in the Actual table, since every ticket starts with AI. Each bot has a distinct closure rate (see botClosureRates).

fields.name: Assigned IT Processor
fields.description: Named human IT support staff member the ticket escalated to. Populated only for escalated tickets.

fields.name: Current Assigned Support
fields.description: Which support tier currently owns the ticket.

fields.name: Current Assigned Name
fields.description: Name of the current owner - either the AI bot name or the human IT processor name, matching Current Assigned Support.

fields.name: Record Type
fields.description: Distinguishes the two tables after a union.

knownCharacteristics.description: Actual and Projection are separate populations and are NOT additive. Union them for side-by-side comparison; never sum them into a single total.

Actual runs 27.6% escalation overall (High 56.8% / Medium 22.9% / Low 22.8%); Projection runs 20.6% (High 51.0% / Medium 16.1% / Low 15.5%). The projection predates the per-bot closure model and was not regenerated, so the plan under-forecasts escalations by roughly 7 points. Regenerate the projection against the current bot model if Plan-vs-Actual escalation parity is needed.
The Projection table has no Assigned AI Bot value, so any bot-level chart must filter to Record Type = Actual.

September 2026 has been cut twice and is now the SMALLEST 2026 month (3,096 vs ~3,150 for Jan-Jun), but it is also lopsidedly open: 2,058 of its 3,096 tickets are open backlog, versus almost none in other months. This is a consequence of the 90-day maximum ticket age plus the 2026-10-01 reference date. Filter to Ticket Status = Closed for a clean monthly creation-volume trend.
2026 Actual covers Jan-Sep only while 2026 Projection covers all 12 months. Any 2026 Plan-vs-Actual comparison is 9 months against 12 unless filtered.
The Projection table begins at 2022. There is no 2021 projection.
Days Open of 0 exists in the Actual table, representing same-day resolutions.
Team Name is assigned independently of Issue Category, so a Hardware ticket can be owned by Cloud Operations. Realistic routing correlation is not modeled.
The city-to-name-origin weighting approximates real population patterns for realism only. It is not census-accurate and must not be used for demographic analysis.

provenance.reproducibilityNote: Each run produces different random draws within the same statistical targets and business rules.
provenance.structuralInspiration: Column shape and a few categorical values were loosely modeled on a public sample help desk dataset; all values here are newly generated.

changes: Renamed the dataset to "AI Chatbot Support Tickets".
Documented resources reduced to the two delivery workbooks: AI Chatbot Support Tickets_Actuals.xlsx and AI Chatbot Support Tickets_Projections.xlsx.
The combined AI Chatbot Support Tickets_Data.xlsx (both tables as two sheets) is redundant with those two and is no longer documented as a primary resource.
No data changes - row counts and distributions are unchanged from 1.2.0.
September 2026 reduced by a further 1,000 tickets (4,096 -> 3,096). The cut came entirely off September closed tickets, so the month is now open-heavy: 2,058 of 3,096 are open backlog.
Actual table regenerated; Projection table again left untouched.
Each AI bot now has a distinct closure rate spread across 58%-85% (previously all six sat at ~84%). Actual table only.
September 2026 volume reduced by 29% (5,769 -> 4,096 tickets created).
Added split single-table workbooks (_Actuals.xlsx, _Projections.xlsx) so each file stays under 25 MB.
Projection table left untouched; it carries no bot assignment and was not regenerated.

botClosureRates.definition: Share of a bot's tickets resolved WITHOUT escalating to a human IT processor.
botClosureRates.appliesTo: Actual table only - the Projection table has no Assigned AI Bot value.
botClosureRates.volumeNote: Ticket volume is split roughly evenly across the six bots (~16.7% each); they differ in outcome, not workload.

additionalFiles.description: Optional convenience file: both tables as two sheets (Actual, Projection) in one workbook. Redundant with the two documented resources above.
